- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate early in horizon; reduce forecast for first 5–7 days.
- After a spike in sentiment (e.g., 1.00), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply dampening factor to 3–5 day forecasts.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is low (≤0.33) and history shows mean reversion; increase forecast slightly for 1–3 days.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model often fails to capture sustained upward momentum; add 10–20% buffer if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment shifts from high to low mid-horizon, model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 10–15% in second half of horizon.
- Model frequently overpredicts in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 2x historical max for first 10 days.
